newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 18.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Security forces personnel will be provided with foreign jobs and employment in the state sector on completion of militry duties, says Major General Srilal Weerasooriya.
The World Bank will assist Sri Lanka to upgrade skills of legal practioners and strengthen legal institutions, says Justice Minister G.L.Peiris.
The government will take action against private institutions employing army and police deserters, says a government spokesmen.
A group of men suspected of being Navy personnel in civil dress assault staff at Colombo's main Pettah bus depot.

A spy plane built in Israel is being used by Sri Lankan security forces to gather information on the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam's operations in the northeastern Wanni jungles, a rebel statement said.
The World Bank will help Sri Lanka reform laws with a view to boosting economic development, says Justice Minsiter G.L. Peiris.
